question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,3]\times [-3,-1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {x}^{2}y-y+5\end{aligned}]. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,-2]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration.
$[$ $4$ {{field-1}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $2$ $]$
$-4\,\,$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
${x}_{1}≈[$ $2.25$ $]$
{{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-y+5) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-y+5)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {x}^{2}y-y+5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -2y \\ 2xy & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{2}+1 \\ {x}^{2}y-y+5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}4(1)^{3} & -2(-2) \\ 2(1)(-2) & {1}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}{1}^{4}-(-2)^{2}+1 \\ (1)^{2}(-2)-(-2)+5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}1.25 \\ -0.75\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}1.25 \\ -0.75\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1.25 \\ -0.75\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2.25 \\ -2.75\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
